name: MathlibAnnex.BilipschitzOrientation.weakDivergenceZero_targetJacobianSign
title: The transported Jacobian sign has zero weak gradient

content.display_title: The transported Jacobian sign has zero weak gradient
content.one_sentence_role: Uses signed transfer and weak Piola with the same test field to obtain the weak equation on the target.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $E=\mathbb R^n$ have the sup norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. Let $S,T\subseteq E$ be open, and let $f,g:E\to E$ be globally Lipschitz maps whose restrictions $f|_S:S\to T$ and $g|_T:T\to S$ are mutually inverse. Fix a number $\ell>0$ such that
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E).$$

Write $Df(x):E\to E$ for the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ when it exists, and set $Df(x)=0$ at other points. Define the signed Jacobian by $J_f(x)=\det Df(x)$.

Define the source sign $s_f:E\to\{-1,1\}$ and its transport $\sigma_f:E\to\{-1,1\}$ by
$$s_f(x)=\begin{cases}1,&J_f(x)\ge0,\\-1,&J_f(x)<0,\end{cases}\qquad \sigma_f(y)=s_f(g(y)).$$
In particular, a zero determinant gives sign $+1$, and $|\sigma_f(y)|=1$ for every $y$.

Let $W:E\to E$ be a $C^1$ vector field that vanishes outside a compact set $K\subseteq T$. Its divergence is $\operatorname{div}W(y)=\operatorname{tr}DW(y)$. With $\lambda$ denoting Lebesgue measure,
$$\int_T\sigma_f(y)\operatorname{div}W(y)\,d\lambda(y)=0.$$
The assertion holds for every such $W$ and $K$.
content.assumptions:
The test field is $C^1$ on all of $E$, and its chosen compact set satisfies $K\subseteq T$ and $W=0$ on $E\setminus K$. Neither connectedness nor finite measure of $T$ is assumed.

The sets $S,T\subseteq E$ are open. The inverse and image conditions are
$$\begin{aligned}
f(S)&\subseteq T,&g(T)&\subseteq S,\\
g(f(x))&=x\quad(x\in S),&f(g(y))&=y\quad(y\in T).
\end{aligned}$$
The global bounds use specified constants $C_f,C_g\ge0$ and $\ell>0$:
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\le C_f\|x-x'\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E),$$
$$\|g(y)-g(y')\|_\infty\le C_g\|y-y'\|_\infty\qquad(y,y'\in E).$$
The estimates hold on all of $E$, not just on $S$ or $T$. The inverse identities are required only on $S$ and $T$.
content.conclusion: The scalar function $\sigma_f$ has zero weak gradient on $T$: its product with the divergence of every admissible test field has integral zero. This is the integral formulation of a weak equation for a scalar function, not the divergence of a vector-valued sign.
content.proof_summary: The divergence of the test field is integrable. Substitute this function into signed transfer; the resulting source integral is zero by weak Piola.

proof_steps.text:
**Verify integrability of the observable.** Put $\phi(y)=\operatorname{div}W(y)$. Then
$$\phi(y)=0\quad(y\notin K),\qquad
\int_E|\phi(y)|\,d\lambda(y)=\int_K|\operatorname{div}W(y)|\,d\lambda(y)<\infty.$$
Indeed, $DW$ is continuous because $W$ is $C^1$, and it vanishes off $K$ because $W$ vanishes locally there. Its trace is therefore continuous and zero off the compact set $K$. This is [integrability of the compact-field divergence](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Piola.lean#L397-L427), applied to this same $W$ and $K$. In particular, $\phi\in L^1(T,\lambda)$.

**Insert the observable into the two integral identities.** The complete substitution is
$$\begin{aligned}
\int_T\sigma_f(y)\operatorname{div}W(y)\,d\lambda(y)
&=\int_T\phi(y)\sigma_f(y)\,d\lambda(y)\\
&=\int_S\phi(f(x))J_f(x)\,d\lambda(x)\\
&=\int_S(\operatorname{div}W)(f(x))J_f(x)\,d\lambda(x)=0.
\end{aligned}$$
The second line is [signed transfer](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L205-L280) with the maps $f,g$, the sets $S,T$, and the observable $\phi=\operatorname{div}W$; Step 1 supplies its integrability hypothesis. The last equality is [weak Piola](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Piola.lean#L375-L395) for the same $f,g,W$ and the inclusion $K\subseteq T$. Since $W$ and $K$ were arbitrary, the weak equation follows.

content.lean_realization_notes: Compactness is imposed on a set outside which the test field vanishes, not on the open set $T$. The statement itself does not require or assert that the sign is constant.
